svg.text: A seven-step spine — evidence, theory, mechanism, politics, vindication — that ends by turning the same scaling
logic on itself and finding it also breeds agency.

g.text: GPT-3's results build a case for scale, which is explained, then tested against who will actually act on it and
vindicated by a decade of wrong predictions — before the same logic is turned on agency itself.

g.title: GPT-3 arrives — 175B params, meta-learning appears — A straightforward scale-up of GPT-2 unexpectedly learns to learn from examples alone. — → spya-dfggb3

Scale alone breeds intelligence — the blessings of scale, generalized — Across vision, games, robotics, and language, bigger models+data+compute reliably yield generalization and meta-learning. — → spya-jwq3zr
Why pretraining works — loss reduction tracks understanding — Minimizing next-token loss forces a model from letter statistics toward genuine world-modeling. — → spya-ce0ts7
Will anyone scale further? — hardware is ready; will is not — DeepMind and Google Brain have the compute but not the conviction to bet everything on scale. — → spya-b6zcpu
g.text: hardware is ready; will is not

g.title: Critics keep being wrong — a decade of failed predictions — Confident 'AI winter' forecasts from respected experts were repeatedly falsified by events. — → spya-bp9mm2
Agency leaks in from data — GPT-3 learns to roleplay agents — Training on human-generated text inevitably teaches a model to imitate goal-pursuing agents. — → spya-hfcz8w
Even formal systems tempt it — cellular automata, Turing machines — Agency-like inference appears even when training on abstract rule systems with no agents at all. — → spya-myjtg3
Backlinks, related pages, bibliography — → spya-g9ffua

g.text: A ladder of ever-subtler linguistic mastery climbing toward human-level loss, with an unresolved doubt hanging off it
and an open question at the top.

g.title: Prediction forces understanding — the pretraining thesis — Humans emit text saturated with logic and causality; predicting it well requires learning those things. — → spya-ce0ts7
First: letters, words, spelling — rapid early gains — Loss drops fast as the model learns letter frequencies, valid words, and simple word associations. — → spya-r465ug
Then: pronouns, coherence — errors shrink, get rarer — Remaining errors become subtler and rarer, like keeping a character's gender pronoun consistent. — → spya-rz8jsm
The last bits are deepest — rare errors, real intelligence — The final fractions of a bit of loss correspond to the rare, consequential judgments that most resemble intelligence. — → spya-kmyg3w
What will GPT-4 unlock? — no one can say — Extrapolating the curve predicts roughly halved loss again, but no one knows what capability that buys. — → spya-uett4g
But is this provable in advance? — reasons for doubt — Similar universal-learning arguments had failed before; only spending the compute actually proved it. — → spya-e5n86h

g.text: A funnel from GPT-3's obvious agency down to a general principle — agency is a cheap, convergent shortcut — then tested
and confirmed even in toy formal systems.

g.title: GPT-3 learns to roleplay agents — Trained on human-generated text, it inevitably learns to imitate goal-pursuing agents when prompted. — → spya-hfcz8w
Agency is built from atoms — no principled boundary — Since agents are made of non-agentic matter, no data can be guaranteed free of agency. — → spya-yb6wsc
We model rivers as agents too — the intentional stance — Humans routinely use teleological, agent-like explanations for non-agentic natural systems. — → spya-frehf0
g.text: We model rivers as agents too

g.title: Systems 'want' to optimize — variational shortcuts — Treating a system as maximizing some quantity is a computationally cheap, powerful shortcut a network could learn. — → spya-tyue6z
But such shortcuts cost compute — only pay off at scale — Variational reasoning only emerges when a problem is rich and repeated enough to beat memorization. — → spya-wkqdua
What data induces agency? — An open empirical question: how much diversity pushes a model from safe modeling into agency. — → spya-ufadea
Game of Life invites 'gliders' — cellular automata — Even a simple rule-based system naturally decomposes into agent-like entities pursuing trajectories. — → spya-myjtg3
What about Turing machines? — Pushed to the most general computational setting: does training on program traces risk agency? — → spya-q88ypt
One machine: just follows rules — no clear agency — A single random Turing machine simply runs; nothing in it is trying to maximize or minimize anything. — → spya-etcjwv
Many machines: infer intent — a rudimentary theory of mind — Meta-learning over many programs forces the model to infer each one's underlying 'intent' from behavior. — → spya-yzb32b
Agency is hard to exclude — like Turing-completeness itself — Agency is a convergent, useful capability; the broader and more powerful the system, the harder it is to keep out. — → spya-c8qwnc
